title: Pendleton to Long Beach

paragraphs.text: In early January 1966, 2/5 prepared to leave Camp Pendleton as a battalion landing team, with artillery, reconnaissance, engineers, motor transport, medical and landing-support elements attached.
The battalion had received 534 enlisted Marines between December 20 and January 8.
Its embarkation table records 1,446 personnel aboard across the landing team, including 1,134 in the reinforced battalion entry.

Getting ready to sail competed with training. Supplies were still reaching Pendleton on January 7, forcing changes to loading plans. Nineteen new M-416-B-1 trailers had arrived, but a lack of spare parts meant older M-100 trailers were embarked as well.
The report lists additional supply blocks, including dry-cell batteries and spare parts, and says the landing team sailed with 93 percent of its operating stocks and mount-out supplies.
The ships were ordered combat-loaded, and cargo for other 1st Marine Division units was added where space allowed.
The landing team's supply officer and supply chief stayed behind to secure the camp, then flew to Okinawa to arrange debarkation.

precision: Arrow shows an illustrative connection between Camp Pendleton and Long Beach, not a verified convoy route. Ship-by-ship personnel and cargo allocations require the referenced sailing reports.
